subject: Point transect encounter rate variances in Distance and mrds

messages.author: 9c6614a1b3d9e242
messages.subject: Point transect encounter rate variances in Distance and mrds
parts:
Good day,

I noticed that although the default estimator of the encounter rate variance among point transects in Program Distance is Fewster et al.'s (2009) varP2 (presented in web appendix B, equation 24), only their varP3 is available to estimate the encounter rate variance for point transects in the 'mrds' R package.

Is there a reason for this?

Our data arise from a camera trap distance sampling survey. The design was systematic (a grid). In spite of this, after reading Fewster et al.'s article and the Web Appendix, I was planning to use varP2 with our data, because the number of "visits" to each point varies, and it does not seem reasonable to assume that the encounter rate is similar throughout the region. Also, from the manual for Program Distance: "Fewster et al. (2009) found that R2 slightly out-performed R3 in simulations, and for this reason as well as because no assumptions are made about animal distribution, this estimator is the default in Distance.... For point transects, the equivalent estimator to R2 is P2."

Eric

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Point transect encounter rate variances in Distance and mrds
parts:
Hi Eric, hi listfolk,

This took a wee bit of digging...

P3 is there because it has exactly the same form as the R3 formula that
was already implemented (so it was easy when we implemented point
transects). As you say, it also handles the important case in which the
number of visits to each point is different. We haven't got around to
implementing all of the estimators yet (though this is on my current
todo list).

Do you know that encounter rate varies over the study area? You could
compute the encounter rate and if that leads you to conclude large
variation in encounter rate then perhaps a geographical (or temporal)
post-stratification scheme might help?


Hope this helps!

cheers,
--dave
